KSH’s 1H2027 profit rises 23% on gains from Singapore condo JVs
article:
KSH Holdings ’ earnings rose 23.3% y-o-y to $6.5 mil for the six months ended Sept 30 (1HFY2027). The increase came mainly from its Singapore residential joint ventures, which moved from losses into profit.

The group’s share of results from associates and joint ventures was a profit of $3.7 mil, compared with a loss of $1.8 mil a year earlier. KSH, which announced its results on Nov 13, credited higher sales and construction progress at its Singapore development projects. The property development segment added $3.2 mil to earnings, up from a $3.7 mil loss in 1HFY2026.

That gain offset weaker results from construction, KSH’s core business. Project revenue rose 22.8% to $75.0 mil on higher work progress, but construction costs rose faster, by $15.5 mil to $63.2 mil. Construction’s contribution to earnings fell to $4.9 mil from $7.2 mil. Group revenue rose 21.7% to $76.8 mil.

KSH has stakes in four Singapore residential projects, all launched and under construction. Its biggest stake (49%) is in the freehold, 172-unit The Arcady at Boon Keng , where 69% of the units have been sold at an average of $2,607 psf, based on caveats lodged with URA Realis as at Nov 15.

KSH also holds a 20% stake in the 440-unit, 99-year leasehold Sora at Yuan Ching Road, which is 55% sold at an average of $2,243 psf. The freehold, 113-unit Bagnall Haus , in which KSH has a 12% stake, is 97% sold at an average of $2,504 psf.

KSH’s smallest stake (10%) is in The Collective at One Sophia , the 367-unit residential component of the One Sophia mixed-use development. The 99-year leasehold project is 26% sold at an average of $2,767 psf.

As at Sept 30, KSH’s share of revenue from units sold but not yet recognised was more than $148 mil. This will be booked as construction progresses.

The group also has stakes in three industrial joint ventures: Gate+ at Tukang Innovation Drive (10%), Tukang Innovation Drive Plot B (30%) and Thomson Gem at Upper Thomson Road (25%). The other two have not been launched yet.

KSH says sales at Gate+, launched in May and now under construction, have been satisfactory. About 46% of its 265 multiple-user factory units have been sold at an average of $605 psf, based on caveats lodged as at Nov 15. Gate+ has a 33-year lease from August 2025.

“Our property development joint venture projects in Singapore and China continue to make steady progress,” says Choo Chee Onn, executive chairman and managing director of KSH. “At the same time, our expansion into industrial properties adds another avenue for growth and further diversifies our property investments.”

In China, sales continued at KSH’s two projects in Singapore Sino Health City, Gaobeidian. Both phases of Zhong Xin Yue Lang are complete. Some 93% of the 812 units in Phase 1 have been sold, as have 37% of the 1,020 units launched in Phase 2.

At Zhong Xin Yue Shang, 98% of the 1,011 units in the completed Phase 1 have been sold. In Phase 2, 94% of the 204 completed units have been sold. A further 1,011 units have been launched, with 12% sold so far, and are slated for completion in FY2027.

Still, China weighed on earnings. Other operating expenses rose $1.8 mil to $4.2 mil, mainly because of a provision for land appreciation tax in China and a loss on the disposal of associates. Rental income from investment properties fell to $1.8 mil from $2.1 mil, owing to lower occupancy and exchange rate effects on rental income from China.

KSH’s construction order book stood at about $887 mil as at Sept 30. The group says this is expected to support its performance through FY2030.

Gearing stood at 0.32 times, with cash and fixed deposits of $142.5 mil. Net asset value per share was 50.89 cents.

title: Smart Reads of the Week: Singapore Bank Earnings, Temasek Stocks, REIT Yields, and US Tech Opportunities
article:
